rounds.text: Service Care Ltd is trading at an attractive valuation with a price-to-earnings ratio of 16.4x, which sits below the sector benchmark of 23.95x [E1, E6]. Fundamental profitability metrics show strength, including a return on capital employed of 10.28% that outpaces the sector benchmark of 8.25%, alongside stellar trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 149% [E10, E19]. The company benefits from a pristine balance sheet, carrying a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.02x and negligible borrowings of Rs 1 Cr [E33, E34]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model calculates an intrinsic value of Rs 153 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 59.6% against the current market price of Rs 61.8 [E40, E41]. Technical indicators confirm strong underlying momentum, with the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages and boasting a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E45, E46]. Conceded: [E30] and [E31], as operating cash flow and free cash flow for March 2026 are negative at Rs -2 Cr and Rs -10 Cr respectively.

Service Care Ltd presents severe underlying cash flow risks that directly contradict any optimistic valuation narrative. Operating cash flow for March 2026 plummeted to negative Rs 2 Cr, resulting in a dismal cash conversion ratio of -0.40x and free cash flow of negative Rs 10 Cr [E29, E30, E31]. Furthermore, top-line growth has ground to a near halt, with compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months crawling at a meager 2% and 3-year growth slowing down to 7% [E16, E15]. Profit quality is also questionable, as earnings are propped up by Rs 2.40 Cr in other income while operating margins remain chronically low at 2% and carry an inconsistent multi-year trend [E25, E27, E59]. Promoter confidence appears to be waning as well, with insider ownership dropping by 7.81 percentage points down to 65.35% since September 2023 [E36], alongside domestic institutional holdings completely vanishing to 0% [E38]. Additionally, the stock offers a 0.00% dividend yield and exhibits high annualised volatility of 45.3% with a poor Sharpe ratio of 0.24, exposing investors to harsh drawdowns that historically reached -56.8% [E4, E48, E49, E50]. Conceded: [E40].
